metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.123

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.123
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.123
- Datum: 04.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, we are somewhat disappointed that Manfred's
exam is but in July, I had wished so much to know you both in Bath.
Meanwhile your teeth will be quite in order and you will feel relieved.
Do not worry about Eva's school. I hope it is quite right for the time being
and in my opinion school-education not so important as home-education
and most of all: self-education. Remember yourself how little we learned in
school of all what later became efficient in our lives and how much by reading
and self-instruction. Eva is in an intelligent milieu and likes reading curi-
ously, so I am not afraid. And for the next term we have plenty of time
to decide as we ourselves have to make decisions. Perhaps we will in the
meantime discontinue to live in Hotels (we are so tired of it) and go somewhere
near to the country provided we will and can stay here; the most important
thing is that you have full confidence in Lotte who is in a certain way
a second mother to Eva and loves her like an own child and you may be
always be sure that we take her education and development as a personal
matter. Lotte told me that Eva would like to have a bicycle, I however do
not favour very much the idea - the time of safe bicycle-riding has gone
and I think it is too dangerous now as all the roads are continually
full of deadly riding cars. I would not feel happy knowing her riding
along these roads, I think it would be better to let play her tennis or
other games which develop the body and are socially useful. Now we have
soon to decide where to go, we prefer to remain near to Newyork, the diffi-
culty is that we dislike Hotels and on the other hand have nobody
for housekeeping and no car, perhaps we will emulate our boy an old
one and tell it again in return. Thanks for the idea to send the Bal-
manuscript. But I could not continue without my reference books
and notes. I am working on my autobiography and one or two little slices
out of it I could sell to Readers Digests which is the best for our own stomach.
I did sent a short story through the British Consulate to Peter Smollet
for his party, I hope it will arrive safely. Lotte is really not suffering
any more but the cure tries to get a definite stop for ever: let us hope that
this ambitious goal will be reached. When this letter will reach you great
decisions - much more important ones than our own - will have been
made here and let us hope the best - how far are the quiet hours we could
pass together; I have always the same wish that you could have at least
Some restful hours in the garden and forget there the bestiality of our age which is not to be reconciled
with the beauty of the eternally peaceful country. And let me repeat: do not be pessimistic and
remind always that all this belongs in reality to you and not to us.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf einem Blatt, beidseitig beschrieben. Der Text am linken Rand wurde quer zum Haupttext geschrieben. Die Tinte ist violett.
